newsitem.title: USA: CME live cattle end firmer as beef prices bottom.
newsitem.headline: CME live cattle end firmer as beef prices bottom.

text.p: CME live cattle futures closed mostly higher when short covering developed following the apparent bottoming in cash beef prices, traders said.

Although lightweight choice boxed beef was quoted only $0.01 per cwt higher at noon, it was the first sign that beef values may have reached a bottom after falling to lowest levels since October 30 on Tuesday. The beef market may be starting to show some retailer interest for post holiday featuring, sources said.
Support came despite added pressure from the sharply lower stock market, they said.

However, early expectations for next week's monthly USDA Cattle-on-Feed report continued to weigh on deferreds at times. Placements of cattle into feedlots remained heavy during November and on-feed supplies are now seen over last year's level, they added.
E.D.& F. Man and RBH bought December and traded both sides of February late. Cargill Investor Services bought February and ADM Investor Services sold December, pit sources said.

In live cattle options, commission houses bought February 68 calls and locals sold 62 puts. Commission houses also sold April 64 puts which lowered volitility in April. Volatility was steady in February, pit sources added.

Feeder cattle continued to follow price swings in deferred live cattle and finished lower but above the day's lows on scattered short covering. However, firming corn futures late and increased numbers of cattle already on feed kept a lid on the market, traders said.
Several Plains-area feedlot managers said their pens are full or near-full currently.
The latest CME feeder cattle index was up $0.30 at $64.83 per cwt.
Live cattle closed 0.175 cent a lb higher to 0.025 lower with February up 0.175 at 62.925 cents. Feeders were off 0.150 to 0.050 with January off 0.075 at 65.900 cents.
